tasks.short: Monitor postoperative animals and notify veterinarians of changes

steps.what: Monitor animals recovering from surgery and assess unusual changes or symptoms
Notify the veterinarian and clarify observed changes and symptoms

tasks.design: Retain direct recovery observation and veterinarian notification. Existing postoperative instructions in {DOCS} guide the assistant; no automatic recovery assessment replaces bedside checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recovery changes require direct observation and clinical escalation.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest supplies no validated animal-recovery automation.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle deterioration and individual animal behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant notices changes and communicates them promptly.
tasks.altitude: No change in monitoring or escalation time.

evidence.claim: Postoperative animal observation and escalation remain human work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is assistant observation and notification, excluding veterinarian treatment and separate charting.
Assistant produces recovery observations in s1's75 hours and clarifies them in s2. No structured deterioration flag or free sensor classification is assumed.
Existing tools remain unchanged; no new upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
unknowns: Animal mix and local observation procedures
research_questions: Which changes require direct observation rather than existing equipment readings alone?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 and zero upkeep; all recovery attention and notification remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify the veterinarian's prescription and the animal and owner identity
Select the prescribed medication and prepare the required quantity
Prepare medication labels from the verified prescription details
Check medication and labels and complete the authorised dispensing handoff

tasks.design: Use native label reuse in {OTHER}, the veterinary practice system, for already verified prescription fields. Retain identity checks, physical preparation and the complete medication and label check; local dispensing authority remains unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verified prescription details may be retyped into labels.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing practice-system templates can copy checked fields without selecting treatment.
tasks.still_hard: Correct product, strength, quantity and directions must match the prescription.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant identifies discrepancies and refers them to the veterinarian.
tasks.altitude: Less label entry; prescribing and dispensing rights do not change.

evidence.claim: Native label copying can reduce repeated entry, but no veterinary dispensing result is supplied by the human-healthcare digest.

assumptions: Boundary is assistant prescription filling, excluding prescribing and any separate veterinarian release check. The existing authorised handoff remains in place.

Veterinarian produces signed animal-specific drug, strength, quantity and directions in unchanged prescribing work. Assistant verifies animal and owner identity and exact fields in s1's30 hours; missing or ambiguous instructions require veterinarian clarification, never inferred doses.
Test native label templates first. No model changes dose or directions; already automatic labels earn no new saving.
unknowns: Local assistant dispensing scope and required final authorisation
research_questions: Does field reuse reduce label work without weakening the final medication check?

already_counted.description: Label review and final preparation check

incremental.description: Maintain label fields and handle copying exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact prepared medication, animal identity, product, strength, quantity and final label directions; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R91 gives9 gross minus2 upkeep net7. Low assumes only2 hours repeated label entry removed; identity30, preparation40 and final check15 remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Examine animals for behavioural changes and clinical symptoms

steps.what: Examine animals for behavioural changes or clinical symptoms indicating illness or injury

tasks.design: Keep direct animal examination with the assistant under the existing veterinary procedure. Reference guidance in {DOCS} supports observation; no behavioural classifier replaces physical checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Subtle signs depend on species and individual baseline behaviour.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest supplies no validated veterinary examination change.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant recognises changes and knows when veterinary review is needed.
tasks.altitude: No change in observation time or diagnostic authority.

evidence.claim: Direct animal examination remains human work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is general animal examination, excluding postoperative monitoring owned by task4306 and veterinarian diagnosis.
Assistant produces observed signs within s1's100 hours. No free structured illness or behavioural-change input is assumed.
No new tool or upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
research_questions: Which changes require comparison with an individual animal's baseline?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 and zero upkeep; all examination effort remains and postoperative work is excluded from this view.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Perform reception duties and schedule appointments

steps.what: Clarify customer requests and capture animal and owner contact details
Find and confirm an appropriate appointment with the customer
Help customers with reception questions and refer clinical concerns

tasks.design: Configure native appointment search in {OTHER}, the veterinary practice system, linked to {CALENDAR}. The assistant clarifies the request, checks the offered appointment and retains customer help and clinical escalation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding slots and copying appointment details can take repeated navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native appointment rules and live availability can narrow slot selection.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent or ambiguous concerns require clinical input.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant listens and escalates instead of turning symptoms into an automated triage decision.
tasks.altitude: Less scheduling navigation; customer interaction and clinical escalation remain.

evidence.claim: Native scheduling can reduce administrative slot search; veterinary reception savings are an unmeasured model scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is assistant reception work, excluding customer time, clinical triage and consultation.

Assistant produces animal and owner identity, contact, stated request and date constraints in s1's30 hours. Practice manager and clinicians maintain approved appointment categories and calendar availability through existing planning work. Assistant resolves uncertain category or urgency manually within retained time; no free structured urgency flag is assumed.
Test native booking configuration first. No autonomous clinical advice or customer bot is introduced.
unknowns: Current booking rules and repeated entry share
research_questions: Does native slot search save time after checking suitability and referring urgent concerns?

already_counted.description: Appointment suitability and exact booking check

incremental.description: Maintain appointment settings and resolve booking exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact appointment animal, owner, service category, clinician, time and confirmation destination; changes void approval
